note: Name-keyed lookup tables whose keys are NOT all flat-lowercase, and therefore CAN be missed by a caller that normalises. Each names the one function allowed to read it. Generated-empty is not the goal: the goal is that every entry here is deliberate. A table with flat-lowercase keys needs no entry, because norm() cannot miss it. See docs/ARTIFACT-ACCESS-RULES.md and tests/test-artifact-keys.js.
not_species_keys: A table flagged here is NOT automatically the MC.mons class. Three of the four families below key camelCase IDENTIFIERS — tag names, feature names, engine counter names — which are minted by one generator and compared verbatim. They trip the FLAT test because norm() would lowercase them, not because anybody normalises them. Saying otherwise would invent a defect. The MC.mons class is a table keyed by a name a HUMAN or a SHEET writes, where two spellings of the same thing exist; that is engine-data.js:MC.mons and porygon2-species.json:mons, and no other entry in this file.

policy-weights featureHashes.features.why: TEN artifacts, ONE answer. Every policy-weights*.json carries a featureHashes block stamped by engine/feature_fixture.js (hashes(dex)), written from engine/fit_policy.js:1372, engine/fit_joint.js:226 or the --stamp CLI. Exactly one function reads the `features` sub-table: verify(), which does `const a = stored[blk]` then `a[f]` for each f in Object.keys(hashes(dex).features). Both sides of that comparison are minted by the same producer — board.js's own feature names via B.FEATURES — so no normalisation exists in the path and no second doorway exists to diverge from. This is R1 working rather than R1 broken: the three callers hand the whole blob to the one reader instead of indexing it themselves (engine/magnemite.js:65 and :450 via checkSemantics, and the `--check FILE` CLI which engine/status.js:365 shells for the refit verdict).
policy-weights featureHashes.features.reachability_stated_rather_than_implied: Two of the ten are read on a routine path: policy-weights.json (engine/status.js:365 and engine/magnemite.js's WEIGHTS_FILE default) and policy-weights-joint.json (engine/magnemite.js's jointWeightsFile default). The other eight are ABLATION and ARCHIVE fits (-all, -joint-presheet, -julyonly, -multiturn, -nomt, -nopop, -pre-censoring, -presheet) and are reached only when somebody passes them explicitly — `node engine/feature_fixture.js --check <file>`, or options.jointWeightsFile. The declaration below is a claim about WHO IS ALLOWED TO READ the table, which is true of all ten; it is NOT a claim that all ten are read today. Recorded here so the entry cannot be quoted as evidence that an ablation stamp is live.
policy-weights featureHashes.features.do_not_edit_the_artifacts: data/policy-weights.json and its siblings are under the owner's pause and are quarantined (fitted on features computed through MEDICHAM). Nothing in this registry modifies them; a restamp is a REFIT question, not a key-convention question.

engine-data.js:MC.mons.why: Keys formes with a hyphen (rotom-wash, slowking-galar) while the project's norm() strips punctuation. 101 of 308 entries were unreachable for weeks, covering 8.17% of observed metagame usage, and it failed silently because a missing key reads as 'never seen this Pokemon'. tests/test-mc-key.js bans hand-rolled lookups into it.

porygon2-species.json:mons.why: Same hyphenated forme keys as MC.mons, so the same mismatch is possible in principle. It has exactly ONE consumer, which also GENERATES the file, so its keys and its lookups cannot diverge today. Listed rather than ignored because a second consumer is precisely the moment this becomes the MC.mons bug again — and at that point this entry is the warning.

scoreboard.json:labels.why: Capitalised keys, but they are DISPLAY LABELS rendered to the page, not identifiers anything looks up by a derived name. Recorded so the detector stays green honestly rather than by narrowing its rule.

tag-consumption.json:by_tag.why: 291 keys, 275 not flat — but they are OUR tag vocabulary (targetClass, formatSecondaryCount, volatileRestart), camelCase identifiers, not species. Sole writer and sole reader are the same file: it writes `by_tag: status` at :349 and reads it back as its own ratchet baseline at :277 (`t in prevStatus`, `prevStatus[t]`). The lookup key `t` comes from Object.keys(uses), built at :62-70 by walking data/tags.json's rec.tags VERBATIM — the identical strings the write side used. No norm() anywhere in the path, and no second consumer: app/ and web/ name the FILE in a quarantine list and read no field of it. Same shape as porygon2-species.json:mons — writer==reader, so keys and lookups cannot diverge today, and this entry is the warning if a second consumer appears.

million-run.json:engine_counters.why: 141 keys, 140 not flat, and they are the field names of the `MEDSEEN` object literal in engine/medicham2-browser.js — code identifiers on BOTH sides, never a name a human or a sheet writes. The one function that INDEXES the table is instrumentChecks(), which reads counters.flinch and counters.secondaryVolatileApplied by hard-coded literal and publishes its verdict beside the table as `instrument_checks`. Same shape as porygon2-species.json:mons and tag-consumption.json:by_tag — writer and reader are the same file, so keys and lookups cannot diverge today, and this entry is the WARNING if a second consumer appears. STATED PRECISELY, so this cannot be quoted as more than it is: instrumentChecks() indexes the live object before the artifact is written, and NOTHING reads the file's copy of the table by key. What reads the file is analysis: docs/_reports/2026-09-04-dead-counters-audit.md classifies 134 counter fields as PROVEN BY RUN and 363 as UNMEASURED purely from which keys are present here, and tests/test-counter-init.js exists BECAUSE this table carried `retaliateWhenLowered: null` in both artifacts — the only non-finite value in either. A table that is the sole record of which engine counters have ever moved is not dead.

deliberately_undeclared.note: EMPTY SINCE 2026-09-06, and the section stays so the reversal below is readable. These are tables that trip the detector and are LEFT RED on purpose. A declaration is a claim that a reader exists; naming one that does not is the citation-shaped failure this repo has already paid for (a figure with a receipt and no source). tests/test-artifact-keys.js reads only `accessors`, so nothing here makes the gate green — that is the intent.

superseded_2026_09_06.what_it_said: million-run.json:engine_counters and million-run-150k.json:engine_counters, both filed 2026-09-04 with the disposition 'DEAD TABLE — nothing reads it' and the remedy 'either give it a named reader, or stop publishing the whole delta'. ROADMAP #539 carried the decision and said the RED was correct and must not be cleared by declaring an accessor.
superseded_2026_09_06.what_refuted_it: The premise was that nothing reads the tables. Two things in this repository read them, and one of them is a test that would not exist otherwise. (1) docs/_reports/2026-09-04-dead-counters-audit.md derives its PROVEN BY RUN / UNMEASURED split — 134 and 363 counter fields — from which keys are present in these two artifacts and nowhere else. (2) tests/test-counter-init.js was written because these two artifacts both carry `retaliateWhenLowered: null`, JSON.stringify(NaN), the only non-finite value in either; its file header cites them by name. The 2026-09-04 finding was true of PROGRAMMATIC readers and it was read as true of all readers.
superseded_2026_09_06.why_the_other_remedy_was_not_taken: Stopping publication cannot clear the red and would destroy that evidence. The gate judges the two files ON DISK. Both were generated 2026-08-11 against release 84f466e7e0d2, both carry `GENERATED — do not hand-edit`, and regenerating them means playing games through MEDICHAM, which is under an ENGINE agent tonight and is the thing under quarantine. So removing the key from the writer would leave the gate red until a re-run, and stripping it from the two artifacts by hand would delete the lines tests/test-counter-init.js cites as its founding evidence. engine/million_run.js is unchanged by this pass.
superseded_2026_09_06.what_is_still_open: The audit's separate proposal — publish `engine_counters_zero` beside the delta, so a counter that stayed at zero is NAMED rather than silently omitted — is untouched here and is not a key-convention question. seenDelta keeps only the keys that MOVED, so this table can never report a zero.
